rationale:
Closes A1's REVISE (s327-A1-pv1000-02-01, reviewedAt 2026-08-21T10:32:01Z) per its own reopenCondition: 'once a worker with src/** authority either rewords i1's predict.reveal to accurately describe what k1 actually does ... and re-pins session301's hash for pv1000-02-01/i1 accordingly'. A1's sole unfixed finding: i1.predict.reveal read 'Hops of ten spin the TENS digit — 2, 3, 4, 5 — while the ones digit stays parked on 0. The hundreds only stir when the tens wrap past 9, which is exactly what the next problem will do.' The claimed 'next problem' is k1 (Skip-count by 100s: 200, 300, 400, ___? -> 500), a hundreds-only count where the tens digit is 0 throughout and never wraps past 9 — it does not demonstrate a tens-into-hundreds rollover at all. That phenomenon first appears two steps later, at i2 (480, 490, ___? -> 500; tens 9->0, hundreds 4->5; immediately preceded by c2's rollover explanation). Verified this reading directly against the lesson JSON's steps array order (c1, i1, k1, c2, i2, c3, i3, k2, k3, ch1, r1) — A1's finding was correct and precise.

Investigated whether the fix is blocked by trio-coordination before touching anything, per this task's mandate. Read src/lib/session273.placeValue1000Course.test.ts in full: for the trio {pv1000-02-01, pv1000-04-02, pv1000-04-03} it pins only (1) each lesson's step-ID sequence array, (2) each lesson's widget-type sequence array (WidgetSpec.parse(item.widget).type over widget-bearing items), and (3) exactly one withheld fixed-exemplar figure per lesson (here: c1.figure===undefined and c1.body contains '320, 330, 340, 350'). The Step type this test operates on ({id, body, figure?, widget?}) has no 'predict' field — the test never reads, hashes, or constrains any step's predict content. i1.widget.type ('numberLineHop'), c1, and the steps array order are all untouched by this fix, so session273's pin cannot be violated by it and no trio-wide coordination is required. Read src/lib/session301.placeValue1000PredictionOrder.test.ts in full: it independently pins, for 12 individual lesson/step pairs spanning the whole place-value-1000 course (one flat row per lesson — not grouped by the session273 trio), each row's canonical option ids, outcomeId, an options-hash, a reveal-hash (SHA-256 of the raw predict.reveal string), and an outcomeIndex parity constraint (index%2+1, a 6/6 split of the correct answer's on-screen slot across the 12 rows). pv1000-04-02 and pv1000-04-03 each have their own independent row (rows 11 and 12) with no structural link to pv1000-02-01's row beyond sharing the same flat array. Confirmed via A1's own already-ledgered KEEP dispositions for both siblings that neither has the analogous defect: A1 explicitly re-checked each sibling's i1.predict specifically because of what was found here ('checked specifically since I found and could NOT fix an analogous dangling predict.reveal at pv1000-02-01') and found pv1000-04-02's reveal 'accurately foreshadows i2's 342-127 ... not a dangling reference' and pv1000-04-03's reveal 'accurate'. Independently confirmed via git diff that neither sibling lesson's predict block appears in this repo's current working-tree diff at all. Conclusion: PATH (a) — a content/prose-only fix confined to one field on one step of one lesson. The only pin actually implicated is session301's single revealHash cell for pv1000-02-01/i1, which A1's own reopenCondition explicitly anticipated and licensed re-pinning. No coordinated trio update, and no edits to pv1000-04-02 or pv1000-04-03, were needed or made — their existing KEEP dispositions (s327-A1-pv1000-04-02, s327-A1-pv1000-04-03) stand unchanged.

FIX: reworded i1.predict.reveal (content/courses/place-value-1000/lessons/pv1000-02-01.json) to 'Hops of ten spin the TENS digit — 2, 3, 4, 5 — while the ones digit stays parked on 0. The hundreds digit only stirs when the tens wrap past 9 — a rollover you'll see demonstrated later in this lesson.' Preserves the first sentence verbatim (already accurate) and the general true rule in the second sentence (hundreds only changes on a tens-past-9 rollover), but drops the false immediate-adjacency claim and replaces it with a claim ('later in this lesson') that stays true regardless of exact step distance, since i2 — five positions later in this same steps array — genuinely demonstrates the rollover. Chose this over A1's alternative remedy (reordering a rollover step to sit immediately next) because reordering would edit the step-ID sequence array session273 pins — a real structural risk this wording-only fix avoids entirely. Re-pinned exactly the implicated cell: session301's pv1000-02-01 contracts row, revealHash field, from 872dd3eec4e5039d8f95417237038f8b1f2fb151617ef500c5d0e682221744cb to ff3571f388aa59ee4b9e23d7dd4627175dea6991db3592881b8699e76d31b3be (verified via a node crypto probe against the exact hash(value)=sha256(value).hex() function the test itself uses, both before editing — confirming the old hash matched the old text — and after). Options, outcomeId, and outcomeIndex parity for this row are byte-identical to before, so optionsHash and the 6/6 parity split are unaffected. Added a 6-line provenance comment directly above the contracts array citing this record and reports/closure/S328_FIX_E3.md. No other file, row, lesson, step ID, widget type, or figure was changed.

Re-verified everything else A1 already verified for this lesson still holds, since nothing else was touched: math for every widget (i1 numberLineHop 320+10*3=350; k1 400+100=500; i2 490+10=500 with rollover; i3 gap-fill 700; k2 backward 280-10=270; k3 300+300=600; ch1 690+10=700; both remedials, already rewritten by A1 earlier in this same session, re-spot-checked: rem-pst elevator-descent 500-10=490, rem-psh stadium-blocks 500+100=600); the withheld-figure resolution (c1 still figure-less, body still contains '320, 330, 340, 350'); and the two registered figures (c2 pv1000-tens-rollover, c3 pv1000-skip-anywhere). visualDecision=SUFFICIENT and gradeLanguageDecision=FIT carried forward unchanged from A1's review — neither touched field affects visual sufficiency, and the new reveal wording is equally grade-2-appropriate, reusing this lesson's own established 'rollover' vocabulary (already used in c2, i2's fallbackFeedback, and rem-pst-k's explanationVariants).

GATES RUN (all targeted/per-file; no full-suite or whole-project commands, per this task's resource constraints): npx vitest run src/lib/session301.placeValue1000PredictionOrder.test.ts src/lib/session273.placeValue1000Course.test.ts — 2 files, 5 tests, all passed. npx vitest run src/lib/session244.causalPredictionSequencing.test.ts (defense-in-depth check for a third possible predict/reveal pin; confirmed pv1000-02-01 does not appear in that file at all, only pv1000-03-02/03-03 do) — 52 tests, all passed. npx tsx scripts/content-check.ts schema — 1840/1840 files clean. npx tsx scripts/content-check.ts pedagogy — 1711/1711 files clean. reviewedBasisHash recomputed post-edit via scripts/session/print-review-basis.mjs pv1000-02-01, run after the content edit landed per its documented byte-sensitivity.
reopenCondition: Reopen if i1's predict.reveal is edited again without re-verifying its forward-reference accuracy against the lesson's then-current step order (specifically: whether some step after i1 still genuinely demonstrates a tens-past-9 rollover into the hundreds digit), or if this lesson's steps array is ever reordered or trimmed such that no later step demonstrates that rollover, or if session301's contracts-row pin mechanism changes in a way that requires this manual re-pin to be re-validated.
